question: The night-shift and day-shift nurses constantly argue over who leaves more work behind. What conflict is this?

options.A: Intergroup conflict
options.B: Interpersonal conflict
options.C: Intragroup conflict
options.D: Intrapersonal conflict

explanation: Since the dispute is between two distinct groups of workers, it's an intergroup conflict. Excellent practice! [learn more](GST321_U5_T3#GST321_U5_T3_h4)

question: What is the main job of the lactiferous sinuses when a mother is breastfeeding?

options.A: They produce the hormone prolactin for milk synthesis
options.B: They filter waste products out of the breast milk
options.C: They secrete lubricating oils to protect the areola
options.D: They temporarily store milk before it reaches the nipple

explanation: Think of lactiferous sinuses as little holding pools right under the dark part of the breast (areola). They keep milk ready right where the baby can easily draw it out. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T10#GNS121_U7_T10_h1)

question: What is the very first step in how cancer starts in the body?

options.A: Chronic dehydration of body tissues
options.B: Excessive intake of dietary proteins
options.C: Rapid spread of bacteria in the blood
options.D: Genetic mutation in a single cell

explanation: Cancer kicks off when a change happens in a cell's genes, making it grow and divide without stopping. You've got this! [learn more](GNS321_U1_T4#GNS321_U1_T4_h1)

question: When does hospice care typically begin for a patient with a terminal illness?

options.A: At the exact moment of diagnosis
options.B: When the patient has about six months or less to live
options.C: Only after the patient loses consciousness
options.D: When family members request discharge home

explanation: Hospice care is designed for individuals who have a prognosis of six months or less if the terminal illness runs its typical course. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T12#GNS321_U4_T12_h1)

question: Which of these is NOT a normal sign of simple pregnancy heartburn?

options.A: Worsening discomfort after eating a large meal
options.B: A sour taste at the back of the throat
options.C: A burning feeling behind the breastbone
options.D: Crushing chest pain radiating to the jaw

explanation: Crushing jaw pain points toward heart trouble, not regular acid reflux. Good clinical spotting! [learn more](GNS226_U2_T013#GNS226_U2_T013_h4)

question: Which side effect is very common after using a rescue inhaler like salbutamol?

options.A: Extreme sleepiness and slow breathing
options.B: Swelling of the feet and ankles
options.C: Fast heart rate and hand tremors
options.D: Severe yellowing of the skin and eyes

explanation: Rescue inhalers stimulate the sympathetic nervous system, which often leaves patients feeling a little jittery with a slightly fast heartbeat. It's totally normal and usually temporary! [learn more](GNS125_U3_T19#GNS125_U3_T19_h5)

question: You are posted to a rural village where women have closely spaced pregnancies. What is the best nursing action?

options.A: Advise community leaders to ban all marriages for young women
options.B: Wait for patients to visit the hospital before discussing reproductive health
options.C: Organize community education on birth spacing and offer family planning counseling
options.D: Focus all clinic resources exclusively on geriatric care programs

explanation: Fantastic! Taking education directly to the community helps families learn about safe birth spacing and maternal health. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T004#GNS226_U6_T004_h7)

question: What does hyperreflexia during a neurological exam usually point to?

options.A: Complete destruction of the sensory receptors in the skin
options.B: A lower motor neuron injury affecting peripheral nerves
options.C: An upper motor neuron lesion in the brain or spinal cord
options.D: Severe dehydration leading to temporary muscle cramps

explanation: Normally, the brain keeps our reflexes in check. When upper motor neurons are damaged, that control is lost, making reflexes overly jumpy (hyperreflexia). [learn more](GNS211_U3_T27#GNS211_U3_T27_h5)

question: What is the primary benefit of connecting a newly diagnosed patient to a peer support group?

options.A: It normalizes their experience and shows them that people can live long, healthy lives with HIV
options.B: It cures the viral infection within a few weeks of consistent meetings
options.C: It provides them with free housing and government food supplies
options.D: It legally waives their responsibility to ever inform their sexual partners

explanation: Peer groups reduce feelings of isolation by introducing patients to others who are thriving despite their diagnosis. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T8#GNS216_U6_T8_h7)

question: How soon can a woman start ovulating again after having an abortion?

options.A: After six months
options.B: After three menstrual cycles
options.C: Within two weeks
options.D: After one year

explanation: Fertility can bounce back as early as two weeks! That's why family planning counseling before discharge is super important. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T008#GNS226_U5_T008_h6)

question: How full should a medical waste bag be before you tie it up and take it away?

options.A: Three-quarters full
options.B: Half full only
options.C: Completely packed to the brim
options.D: One-quarter full

explanation: You got it! Stopping at three-quarters full leaves you enough space to securely tie the bag shut without risking nasty tears or accidental punctures. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T5#GNS122_U5_T5_h3)

question: What is the single most effective way to stop the spread of hospital infections?

options.A: Proper hand hygiene
options.B: Wearing sterile boots
options.C: Changing bed sheets daily
options.D: Spraying room air freshener

explanation: Frequent and thorough handwashing or alcohol rubbing removes transient microorganisms and stops them from passing between patients. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T7#GNS112_U4_T7_h3)

question: What is the purpose of performing a bimanual examination right before an MVA starts?

options.A: To determine the exact size and position of the uterus
options.B: To scrape away loose tissue without needing a canula
options.C: To check if the patient's bladder is completely empty
options.D: To measure the patient's blood pressure and pulse rate

explanation: Knowing whether the uterus is tilted forward or backward helps the clinician guide instruments smoothly and prevents accidental perforation. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T010#GNS226_U5_T010_h5)

question: When wiping a bedside table in the ward, what direction should a nurse move?

options.A: From the cleanest area to the dirtiest area
options.B: Starting at the floor and moving upward
options.C: From the bottom edges up to the top center
options.D: In random circles across the entire surface

explanation: Smart nursing habit! Moving from clean to dirty ensures you aren't dragging grime and germs right back onto the spotless parts of the table. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T5#GNS122_U2_T5_h6)

question: Why is exact timing so important for blood draws during dynamic hormone tests?

options.A: Blood samples spoil if they sit at room temperature
options.B: Hormones disappear from the blood after five minutes
options.C: Laboratory technicians only work during morning hours
options.D: Hormone levels shift rapidly in response to specific triggers

explanation: Hormones react fast! Precise timing lets us catch the exact moment the gland reacts to our test medicine. [learn more](GNS211_U1_T8#GNS211_U1_T8_h5)

question: Which of these is NOT a typical result of eating a lot of junk food or processed snacks during adolescence?

options.A: Poor long-term bone health
options.B: Stronger skeletal bone density
options.C: Increased risk of iron deficiency
options.D: Erratic eating schedules

explanation: Processed foods lack key nutrients like calcium, so they certainly won't build stronger bones! [learn more](GNS227_U2_T007#GNS227_U2_T007_h6)

question: What does the FIFO stock rotation rule stand for?

options.A: Free-Issue, Fixed-Order
options.B: Final-Inspection, First-Order
options.C: First-In, First-Out
options.D: Fast-Item, Fast-Out

explanation: FIFO means the items that arrived first on the shelf should be the ones picked and used first. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T19#GNS122_U3_T19_h3)

question: In the HEADS adolescent screening tool, what does the letter 'S' stand for?

options.A: Skeletal strength
options.B: Sexuality
options.C: Sleep hygiene
options.D: Skin integrity

explanation: Spot on! In HEADS, 'S' stands for Sexuality (and Suicide), guiding the nurse to check in on relationships and reproductive health. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T5#GNS312_U3_T5_h6)

question: What is a simple, cheap way villagers can stop themselves from swallowing Guinea worm larvae in their drinking water?

options.A: Adding tablespoons of cooking oil to the water
options.B: Exposing the water bucket to direct moonlight
options.C: Stirring the water vigorously with a wooden spoon
options.D: Filtering water through a clean cloth

explanation: You got it! A simple cloth filter catches the tiny fleas carrying the larvae. Public health nursing is often about simple, effective tools! [learn more](GNS313_U2_T23#GNS313_U2_T23_h8)

question: What color should a healthy mother's lochia look like during the first three days after delivery?

options.A: Bright red color
options.B: Clear watery consistency
options.C: Green foul-smelling discharge
options.D: Creamy white color

explanation: In the beginning, lochia is called 'rubra' (red) because it's mostly fresh blood and tissue. Completely normal for the first few days! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T52#GNS214_U1_T52_h3)

question: Which rhythm shows a messy, chaotic baseline with no clear P waves and an all-over-the-place heartbeat?

options.A: Atrial fibrillation
options.B: First-degree heart block
options.C: Sinus bradycardia
options.D: Sinus tachycardia

explanation: In A-fib, the atria just quiver instead of squeezing properly, giving us that messy, irregular baseline. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T16#GNS213_U1_T16_h6)

question: Why is it important to keep cardboard safety boxes away from damp floors?

options.A: Moisture helps safety boxes assemble themselves
options.B: Water makes the needles inside sharper and safer
options.C: Wet cardboard attracts helpful insects to the room
options.D: Dampness weakens the cardboard and causes dangerous leaks

explanation: That's right! Water ruins cardboard rigidity, which can lead to nasty punctures or fluid leaks from used sharps. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T12#GNS122_U3_T12_h6)

question: Beyond physical checks, what is another crucial part of postpartum care for a mother who just had twins or triplets?

options.A: Encouraging the mother to return to work within two weeks
options.B: Restricting family visits to prevent the mother from talking
options.C: Providing emotional support and connecting them with practical resources
options.D: Insisting that the mother cares for the newborns entirely on her own

explanation: Well done! Raising more than one baby at once can feel overwhelming. Offering kind words and connecting families to helper networks is a huge part of great nursing care. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T018#GNS226_U2_T018_h7)

question: What is the main goal of giving post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) right after an accidental needle stick?

options.A: To cure a chronic bacterial skin infection
options.B: To prevent the establishment of a viral infection
options.C: To numb the skin and prevent local tissue scarring
options.D: To relieve muscle spasms around the injury site

explanation: PEP uses quick antiviral meds to stop a virus from taking hold and multiplying after an accidental exposure. Every minute counts! [learn more](GNS122_U3_T4#GNS122_U3_T4_h7)

question: Which surprising non-food item can also pack a hidden load of sodium for patients?

options.A: Effervescent medications and dissolvable antacids
options.B: Plastic IV catheters used for hydration
options.C: Standard cotton hospital gowns and bedding
options.D: Topical skin moisturizers and lotions

explanation: You nailed it! Medicines that fizz and dissolve in water often use sodium compounds to get that reaction, adding sneaky sodium to the day. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T008#GNS227_U6_T008_h4)

question: What is the primary goal of using aseptic techniques during immunization?

options.A: To prevent the introduction of harmful pathogens into the body
options.B: To make the injection completely painless for the client
options.C: To speed up the total vaccination process
options.D: To ensure the vaccine liquid remains ice cold

explanation: Aseptic techniques are specifically designed to stop germs from contaminating sterile equipment and entering the client's body during a procedure. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T67#GNS214_U1_T67_h1)

question: What critical instruction must a nurse give a patient before they apply a fresh transdermal patch?

options.A: Apply the new patch directly on top of the old patch
options.B: Wash the old patch with soap and leave it in place
options.C: Remove the old patch before putting on the new one
options.D: Cut the new patch in half to double the lifespan

explanation: Leaving an old patch on while applying a new one causes dangerous drug overdosing because medication continues to absorb from both patches. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T16#GNS125_U3_T16_h8)

question: When you help a patient with their personal hygiene, why is it considered a special nursing care rather than just a normal house chore?

options.A: It replaces the need to give prescribed drugs
options.B: It is the only duty a nurse can leave for relatives
options.C: It allows the nurse to assess the skin and build trust
options.D: It guarantees the patient will feel zero pain

explanation: Spot on! Washing and grooming put you close enough to spot early skin changes and build a warm, trusting relationship with your patient. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T1#GNS112_U5_T1_h1)

question: A patient eats a snack with 10g of carbs, 5g of protein, and 4g of fat. What is their total calorie intake?

options.A: 60 kcal
options.B: 96 kcal
options.C: 76 kcal
options.D: 19 kcal

explanation: Let's break it down: Carbs (10 x 4 = 40), Protein (5 x 4 = 20), Fat (4 x 9 = 36). Add them up (40 + 20 + 36) to get 96 total calories. You're doing great with math! [learn more](GNS227_U4_T007#GNS227_U4_T007_h3)

question: Which service would you most expect to find at a local primary health care center?

options.A: Sub-specialty pediatric neurology consultations
options.B: Advanced cancer chemotherapy and radiation therapy
options.C: Routine childhood immunization and antenatal care
options.D: Complex open-heart surgical procedures

explanation: Primary health centers focus heavily on community wellness. That means giving babies their routine vaccines and supporting mothers with antenatal care every day! [learn more](GNS112_U2_T2#GNS112_U2_T2_h2)

question: At what centimeter of cervical dilation does the alert line begin on a standard WHO partograph?

options.A: 7 centimeters
options.B: 2 centimeters
options.C: 10 centimeters
options.D: 4 centimeters

explanation: You're doing amazing! The partograph alert line starts ticking once active labour gets going at 4 cm dilation. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T006#GNS226_U3_T006_h8)

question: Why is nursing care during the puerperium so important for a new mother?

options.A: It ensures the mother avoids all postpartum sadness
options.B: It prevents sudden complications like hemorrhage and infection
options.C: It eliminates the need for any follow-up doctor visits
options.D: It guarantees the infant will sleep through the night

explanation: You've got this! Regular checks in the postpartum period help catch physical problems early, keeping the new mother safe and healthy during her recovery. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T010#GNS226_U1_T010_h1)

question: What is the single most important thing a nurse can do to stop infections from spreading?

options.A: Performing thorough hand hygiene
options.B: Administering daily multivitamins
options.C: Keeping all windows wide open
options.D: Changing bed sheets once a week

explanation: Never underestimate good handwashing! It is our #1 weapon as nurses against hospital-acquired infections. [learn more](GST114_U2_T2#GST114_U2_T2_h7)

question: If a patient gets infected through a mosquito bite, what type of transmission is this?

options.A: Feco-oral route
options.B: Vector-borne transmission
options.C: Direct skin penetration
options.D: Congenital transmission

explanation: Easy peasy! A 'vector' is like a living taxi (like a mosquito) that carries the parasite from one person to another. [learn more](GST114_U6_T2#GST114_U6_T2_h4)

question: Which type of vitamin is most likely to cause toxicity if taken in excess because they store up in body fat?

options.A: Amino acid supplements
options.B: Water-soluble vitamins
options.C: B-complex vitamins
options.D: Fat-soluble vitamins

explanation: Vitamins A, D, E, and K dissolve in fat and hang around in the body instead of being flushed out in urine. Too much of a good thing can be harmful! [learn more](GNS227_U7_T014#GNS227_U7_T014_h5)

question: What heart action directly causes the apex beat you feel on the chest?

options.A: Filling of the right atrium during diastole
options.B: Closure of the aortic and pulmonary valves
options.C: Contraction of the left ventricle during systole
options.D: Opening of the tricuspid and mitral valves

explanation: When the left ventricle squeezes, it twists forward and taps against the chest wall, creating that palpable apex beat. [learn more](GNS112_U6_T2#GNS112_U6_T2_h6)

question: Where in the skin are Langerhans cells mostly found?

options.A: The subcutaneous fat
options.B: The hypodermis
options.C: The sweat ducts
options.D: The epidermis

explanation: Spot on! They hang out right in the epidermis so they can easily catch any germs trying to sneak in from the outside. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T3#GNS211_U2_T3_h4)

question: What is a major giveaway that a digital blood pressure cuff has an air leak?

options.A: The screen flashes bright red and rings a loud alarm
options.B: The battery icon shows full charge the whole time
options.C: The machine shows an error code or cannot finish pumping up
options.D: The device measures the blood pressure twice as fast as usual

explanation: If air is escaping, the machine can't build up the pressure it needs, so it will usually flash an error message at you. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T1#GNS212_U4_T1_h5)

question: What is the main purpose of a reflex arc?

options.A: To allow the cerebral cortex to consciously plan complex body movements
options.B: To transmit deep thought processes from the frontal lobe to organs
options.C: To control an involuntary, rapid response to protect the body from harm
options.D: To store long-term memories in the peripheral nervous system

explanation: Reflexes are your body's built-in safety system! They trigger super-fast, automatic reactions—like pulling your hand away from a hot stove—before you even have time to think. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T16#GNS211_U3_T16_h5)

question: Which of the following is NOT a safe condition for a home delivery?

options.A: Singleton pregnancy
options.B: Head-down baby position
options.C: Normal blood pressure
options.D: Placenta previa

explanation: Placenta previa causes severe bleeding and requires immediate hospital management, making home delivery extremely dangerous. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T9#GNS225_U3_T9_h4)

question: What is the normal pH range for human blood?
explanation: Human blood must stay within a very narrow alkaline range of 7.35 to 7.45 for normal body enzymes to function. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T12#GNS121_U2_T12_h1)

question: What should be your very first priority when nursing a survivor of gender-based violence?

options.A: Demanding that the survivor immediately file a police report before treatment
options.B: Providing compassionate medical care, physical safety, and emotional support
options.C: Telling the patient to forget the incident and focus on daily chores
options.D: Refusing to document physical injuries to protect the hospital from lawsuits

explanation: A survivor's safety, physical healing, and gentle emotional support always come first in clinical nursing. Make them feel safe and heard! [learn more](GNS216_U1_T3#GNS216_U1_T3_h8)

question: Why do people with severe malabsorption often look pale, feel very tired, and bruise easily?

options.A: Bile pigment backs up into the subcutaneous fat tissue and stains the skin
options.B: The liver stops producing red blood cells because the stomach is empty
options.C: Undigested food proteins enter the bloodstream and destroy white blood cells
options.D: Malabsorption prevents proper uptake of vital elements like iron, folate, and fat-soluble vitamins needed for blood health

explanation: Without healthy villi, the body misses out on iron, B12, and vitamin K, which leads directly to anemia and easy bleeding. Brilliant clinical thinking! [learn more](GNS213_U3_T8#GNS213_U3_T8_h5)

question: Why should nurses participate in emotional debriefing after handling multiple patient deaths?

options.A: To fulfill mandatory hospital financial auditing rules
options.B: To prevent emotional burnout and maintain mental well-being
options.C: To practice their clinical writing and documentation skills
options.D: To learn how to avoid making errors on death certificates

explanation: Regularly dealing with loss takes an emotional toll, making peer support and debriefing essential for nursing self-care. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T10#GNS221_U4_T10_h6)

question: Why is it important to ensure that traction weights hang freely off the bed?

options.A: Hanging weights prevent the patient from moving their upper body
options.B: Touching the floor causes the traction ropes to snap in half
options.C: Resting weights on the floor increases the patient's blood pressure
options.D: Touching the floor disrupts the steady pulling force on the bone

explanation: Traction requires continuous, unobstructed tension to keep bone fragments aligned; if weights touch the floor, that tension is lost. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T10#GNS222_U1_T10_h8)

question: Which action shows that a nurse is truly practicing active listening?

options.A: Giving full attention and minimizing distractions
options.B: Interrupting to offer quick medical solutions
options.C: Looking around the room for the next client
options.D: Writing in a chart while the patient speaks

explanation: Active listening means putting other tasks aside and showing the patient they have your complete, caring focus. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T11#GNS124_U5_T11_h6)

question: What is the primary reason for recommending a low-sodium diet in cardiac prevention?

options.A: It prevents the liver from producing too much cholesterol
options.B: It reduces fluid retention and lowers blood pressure
options.C: It stops the pancreas from releasing excess insulin
options.D: It increases the amount of dietary fiber in the gut

explanation: Excess sodium holds extra fluid in the blood vessels, increasing the pressure against arterial walls and forcing the heart to work harder. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T15#GNS213_U1_T15_h3)

question: What is the main reason why medication rooms in the ward must always be kept locked?

options.A: To prevent unauthorized access and accidental drug mix-ups
options.B: To make it difficult for doctors to write new prescriptions
options.C: To keep the air conditioning inside the room very cold
options.D: To hide hospital supply costs from incoming student nurses

explanation: Locking the drug room keeps powerful medications safe from unauthorized people and helps keep everything organized for the team. [learn more](GNS125_U4_T1#GNS125_U4_T1_h3)

question: You feel a new mother's uterus and notice it feels soft, boggy, and pushed to the right. What should you do right away?

options.A: Prepare the patient for immediate surgery
options.B: Administer a dose of oral iron tablets
options.C: Encourage the mother to empty her bladder
options.D: Apply a warm compress to the lower back

explanation: Wonderful clinical thinking! A full bladder often pushes the womb out of place and stops it from tightening up. Once she pees, the womb usually firms right back up! [learn more](GNS226_U3_T006#GNS226_U3_T006_h7)

question: What is the primary purpose of using the topical route of administration?

options.A: To guarantee immediate intravenous bloodstream entry
options.B: To force rapid first-pass liver metabolism of the drug
options.C: To treat a local condition directly on a body surface
options.D: To bypass the need for any skin or mucous membrane contact

explanation: Topical medications are primarily applied directly to the skin or mucous membranes to treat surface-level issues right where they are placed. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T16#GNS125_U3_T16_h1)

question: Why is a Pap smear so important when you spot a red patch on the cervix?

options.A: To chemically destroy the extra columnar cells on the surface
options.B: To measure the exact hormonal levels circulating in the bloodstream
options.C: To rule out malignant or pre-cancerous changes that can look similar to benign erosion
options.D: To prove that the patient has an active bacterial infection

explanation: Harmless ectropion can sometimes look very similar to early cellular changes or cancer. A Pap smear helps us be 100% sure the patient is safe. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T17#GNS216_U5_T17_h7)

question: Which environmental issue is currently one of the biggest threats to farming and food supplies?

options.A: Strict government food safety regulations
options.B: Decreased global demand for fresh vegetables
options.C: Excessive use of indoor community gardens
options.D: Climate change and erratic weather patterns

explanation: Unpredictable rains, extreme droughts, and severe floods ruin crops globally, making it harder for farmers to keep up food production. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T029#GNS227_U2_T029_h7)

question: What is polyspermy?

options.A: The rapid division of cells before implantation
options.B: The natural death of the oocyte inside the ovary
options.C: The fertilization of an oocyte by more than one sperm
options.D: The complete absence of sperm in the ejaculate

explanation: Polyspermy happens when multiple sperm enter an egg, which causes a dangerous overload of chromosomes that stops healthy development. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T1#GNS121_U6_T1_h5)

question: What should a nurse do FIRST immediately after discovering a medication error has occurred?

options.A: Call the hospital security department to investigate
options.B: Hide the incident report form so nobody finds out
options.C: Leave the ward immediately to avoid disciplinary action
options.D: Assess the patient's clinical condition and provide necessary care

explanation: Patient safety and immediate clinical evaluation always take priority over paperwork or administrative reporting when an error happens. [learn more](GNS125_U4_T2#GNS125_U4_T2_h8)

question: Why is a sputum culture ordered when a client has a persistent productive cough?

options.A: To identify the specific microorganism causing an infection
options.B: To measure the total daily volume of mucus production
options.C: To check if the client has smoked cigarettes recently
options.D: To evaluate how well the lungs exchange gases

explanation: Culturing mucus allows the laboratory to grow the infectious agent and determine which antibiotic will treat it best. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T2#GNS213_U2_T2_h5)

question: An older male patient with an enlarged prostate experiences constant urinary dribbling because his bladder is completely full. What is this called?

options.A: Overflow incontinence
options.B: Urge urinary incontinence
options.C: Stress urinary incontinence
options.D: Functional incontinence

explanation: When a blockage stops the bladder from emptying properly, it overfills and leaks small amounts. We call this overflow incontinence. Excellent nursing insight! [learn more](GNS121_U2_T9#GNS121_U2_T9_h6)

question: Which category of substances acts by slowing down brain activity and central nervous system functions?

options.A: Stimulants
options.B: Hallucinogens
options.C: Inhalants
options.D: Depressants

explanation: Correct! Depressants like alcohol put the brakes on the nervous system, which can dangerously lower breathing and heart rates if taken in excess. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T4#GNS313_U3_T4_h2)

question: A 16-year-old girl visits your clinic for family planning advice but is terrified her parents will find out. How should you respond as a nurse?

options.A: Scold her for engaging in premarital relationships
options.B: Refuse service and call her parents immediately
options.C: Assure her of confidentiality and provide age-appropriate counseling
options.D: Report her to local law enforcement authorities

explanation: Trust is everything in nursing! By assuring her of confidentiality, you make her feel safe enough to get the right health education and protection instead of hiding risky situations. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T4#GNS216_U1_T4_h5)

question: Why must you clean connection hubs with an alcohol swab before changing lines?

options.A: It ensures the plastic tubing remains soft and flexible
options.B: It makes the digital screen easier to read in bright light
options.C: It removes sticky residue left behind by medical tape
options.D: It prevents microbes from entering the bloodstream and causing infection

explanation: Spot on! Good aseptic technique keeps nasty bacteria from hitching a ride directly into your patient's bloodstream. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T4#GNS212_U4_T4_h7)

question: A patient with suspected polyneuropathy has blood drawn for routine laboratory tests. Which underlying condition is the nurse primarily helping to screen for with tests like HbA1c?

options.A: Bacterial meningitis
options.B: Diabetes mellitus
options.C: Multiple sclerosis
options.D: Parkinson's disease

explanation: Checking fasting blood sugar and HbA1c is a priority diagnostic step because diabetes is the leading cause of peripheral neuropathy. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T18#GNS222_U3_T18_h5)

question: Why might an elderly patient with osteomyelitis not have a high fever?

options.A: Circulating antibiotics constantly suppress core body temperature
options.B: Their immune response may be blunted, altering classic systemic signs
options.C: Bone infections never cause systemic temperature changes in adults
options.D: Older bones are completely immune to inflammatory pyrogens

explanation: Older adults sometimes have quieter immune systems, meaning they might not show the textbook high fever even when a serious infection is brewing. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T18#GNS222_U1_T18_h4)

question: A patient had severe, untreated salpingitis a year ago. What long-term change is most likely in her fallopian tubes now?

options.A: Thinned muscle walls and widened openings
options.B: Enlarged and overly active cilia hairs
options.C: Narrowed lumens and scar tissue adhesions
options.D: Complete disappearance of the fimbriae

explanation: Past severe inflammation leaves behind scar tissue that can narrow the inside passageway (lumen) of the tube. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T24#GNS216_U5_T24_h3)

question: Why must patients take their hormone replacement medication for life?

options.A: Stopping the drug suddenly cures the underlying condition
options.B: Glands regenerate faster if they do not receive pills
options.C: Medications build up toxic stores in the liver over time
options.D: The body cannot naturally make up for the missing hormone

explanation: Since the gland can't fix itself or make the hormone anymore, the patient needs ongoing help from daily medicine to stay healthy. [learn more](GNS211_U1_T8#GNS211_U1_T8_h6)

question: Why must you give careful discharge advice to a chemical exposure patient who currently looks and feels completely fine?

options.A: Some chemical injuries and pulmonary complications develop hours later
options.B: Most chemical exposures become contagious after twenty-four hours
options.C: Delayed blood tests are legally required to be performed at home
options.D: Hospital policy requires patients to read safety manuals at home

explanation: Some poisons play the long game. Tissue damage can pop up hours after the exposure, so patients need to know what warning signs to watch for at home. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T5#GNS215_U5_T5_h6)

question: A bedridden patient has a red spot on their lower back that doesn't fade when pressed. As a nurse, what should you do first?

options.A: Implement a strict turning schedule and use a pressure-relieving surface
options.B: Restrict daily fluid intake to reduce local tissue edema
options.C: Apply strong antiseptic ointment directly over the red skin area
options.D: Massaged the reddened spot vigorously to stimulate blood flow

explanation: That red spot is an early pressure ulcer warning! Taking the pressure off by turning the patient is your best first move. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T16#GNS222_U4_T16_h6)

question: Why does your nose feel so stuffy and congested when you catch a cold?

options.A: Inflammatory mediators cause local blood vessels to dilate and leak fluid into tissues
options.B: Infiltrating bacteria block the normal flow of air through the sinus passages
options.C: The nasal cartilage permanently expands in response to cold temperatures
options.D: Inhaled dust particles accumulate rapidly because cilia stop growing

explanation: When your immune system fights a cold virus, blood vessels in your nose widen and swell up, letting fluid leak into the tissues. This narrows your airway and creates that annoying stuffy feeling! [learn more](GNS311_U3_T6#GNS311_U3_T6_h2)

question: What exactly is a 'sampling frame' in research?

options.A: The final group of patients selected for a clinical trial
options.B: The statistical formula used to calculate sample size
options.C: A physical list of all eligible members in a target population
options.D: A barrier preventing patients from joining a study

explanation: You got it! Think of the sampling frame as your actual register, directory, or database from which you pull your participants. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T18#GNS224_U1_T18_h2)

question: Why must a needle-stick injury be reported to the infection control team right away?

options.A: To prove that the nurse was not paying attention to work
options.B: To make sure the patient gets charged extra hospital fees
options.C: To schedule a mandatory disciplinary hearing for the ward
options.D: To ensure quick medical review and timely post-exposure treatment

explanation: Medicines to prevent infection work best when taken within hours, so reporting it fast is super important for your health. [learn more](GST114_U2_T8#GST114_U2_T8_h7)

question: Which of the following is NOT considered a harmful traditional practice?

options.A: Female genital mutilation performed without anesthesia
options.B: Forced physical practices during early puberty rites
options.C: Routine childhood immunizations against measles
options.D: Child marriage involving underage adolescents

explanation: Immunizations save children's lives from deadly diseases! They are a standard, safe medical intervention, unlike harmful cultural practices. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T3#GNS216_U1_T3_h8)

question: How does the parasympathetic system help control your urinary bladder?

options.A: It tightens all sphincters so you never pee
options.B: It relaxes the bladder wall to hold more urine
options.C: It contracts the bladder wall to help you pass urine
options.D: It has no role in urinary control

explanation: Parasympathetic stimulation tells the bladder wall (detrusor muscle) to squeeze and the internal sphincter to relax so urine can flow out. Excellent nursing knowledge! [learn more](GNS211_U3_T31#GNS211_U3_T31_h5)

question: Which type of lubricant can damage and weaken a latex diaphragm?

options.A: Water-soluble jelly
options.B: Natural saliva
options.C: Spermicidal creams
options.D: Oil-based lubricants

explanation: Oils and petroleum jelly break down latex rubber super fast, creating weak spots and tears. Always stick to water-based lubes! [learn more](GNS226_U6_T017#GNS226_U6_T017_h6)

question: Which white blood cells shoot up in number during a parasitic worm infection?

options.A: Erythrocytes
options.B: Platelets
options.C: Eosinophils
options.D: Osteoclasts

explanation: Eosinophils are your body's specialized fighters against parasites like worms, and they also help calm down allergic reactions. [learn more](GST114_U2_T3#GST114_U2_T3_h8)

question: During a measles outbreak, why do public health teams do 'contact tracing'?

options.A: To collect financial penalties for spreading the infection
options.B: To monitor exposed individuals during the incubation period and offer vaccination
options.C: To test the water supply for bacterial contamination
options.D: To punish individuals who failed to attend the primary health clinic

explanation: Great clinical thinking! Tracing contacts lets nurses catch infections early and vaccinate people before symptoms appear. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T16#GNS313_U1_T16_h7)

question: What is a common health problem in children who eat a poor, low-diversity diet?

options.A: Complete immunity to common childhood tropical diseases
options.B: Rapid increase in bone density and excessive height
options.C: Sudden development of high blood pressure in infancy
options.D: Increased vulnerability to infections and stunted physical growth

explanation: That's right. Missing out on diverse nutrients weakens their immune system and slows down their growth, leading to frequent illnesses. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T004#GNS227_U2_T004_h5)

question: Out of the common types of vaginitis, which one is officially classified as a sexually transmitted infection (STI)?

options.A: Atrophic vaginitis
options.B: Trichomoniasis
options.C: Vulvovaginal candidiasis
options.D: Bacterial vaginosis

explanation: Trichomoniasis is caused by a tiny parasite and is primarily passed along through sexual contact. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T10#GNS216_U5_T10_h2)

question: Which of these is NOT a good strategy for promoting gender-sensitive nursing care?

options.A: Considering both biological factors and social pressures during assessment
options.B: Using respectful and inclusive language during patient history collection
options.C: Making automatic assumptions about a patient's health needs based purely on their gender
options.D: Advocating for equitable healthcare access across all segments of society

explanation: Spot on! Good nursing care means treating every patient as a unique individual, not making assumptions based on gender stereotypes. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T2#GNS312_U4_T2_h7)

question: What do we call the emotional exhaustion and stress that nurses feel from constantly caring for sick and suffering patients?

options.A: Bereavement overload
options.B: Anticipatory grief
options.C: Actual loss syndrome
options.D: Compassion fatigue

explanation: Well done! Compassion fatigue is real—it's what happens when the emotional weight of caring for others starts draining your own energy and empathy. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T9#GNS321_U4_T9_h8)

question: Which action shows that you are using good body mechanics while making a bed?

options.A: Keeping the hospital bed in its lowest position throughout the procedure
options.B: Stretching your arms far across the mattress without moving your feet
options.C: Using leg muscles with a wide base of support when moving heavy items
options.D: Twisting rapidly at the waist to transfer linen from one hand to the other

explanation: Wonderful! Using your legs and keeping a wide stance protects your back from injury during nursing duties. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T3#GNS112_U4_T3_h6)

question: Which of the following activities must a client avoid during the GTT waiting period?

options.A: Drinking small sips of plain water
options.B: Smoking cigarettes or drinking coffee
options.C: Sitting quietly in a comfortable chair
options.D: Reading a book or magazine

explanation: Nicotine and caffeine stimulate the nervous system and can alter blood glucose readings, so they are strictly prohibited. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T20#GNS222_U2_T20_h6)

question: Why does involving religious and community leaders help overcome vaccine hesitancy?

options.A: They hold trusted positions of influence within the community
options.B: They control the distribution budget for local health clinics
options.C: They are legally trained to administer vaccines in public
options.D: They personally manufacture the vaccines used in primary care

explanation: Spot on! Community members listen closely to spiritual leaders, so their support is powerful for clearing up health misconceptions. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T69#GNS214_U1_T69_h2)

question: Why do we encourage regular walking for patients with stable Peripheral Artery Disease?

options.A: It lowers the total volume of blood circulating in the body.
options.B: It immediately dissolves any deep vein blood clots in the legs.
options.C: It helps develop collateral blood vessels around blocked arteries.
options.D: It forces existing fatty plaque out through the capillary bed.

explanation: Exercise is amazing here! Gentle walking encourages the body to build tiny 'detour roads' (collateral vessels) to bypass the blocked main arteries. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T5#GNS123_U5_T5_h7)

question: How soon can a woman start ovulating and get pregnant again after an abortion?

options.A: Only after six months of complete amenorrhea
options.B: After her third normal menstrual cycle
options.C: Not until she reaches menopause
options.D: As early as two weeks post-abortion

explanation: Fertility bounces back super fast! That is why family planning counseling before discharge is a vital part of nursing care. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T003#GNS226_U5_T003_h8)

question: What is the main purpose of a comprehensive pediatric assessment after a positive screening?

options.A: To establish a clear diagnosis and guide treatment planning
options.B: To replace the need for routine childhood immunizations
options.C: To prove that developmental delays are always temporary
options.D: To discharge the patient from the healthcare system permanently

explanation: A thorough assessment provides the specific medical and developmental diagnosis needed to build an effective care plan. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T6#GNS225_U5_T6_h3)

question: What is the main job of the plastic sheet found in a standard birth kit?

options.A: To provide a clean, moisture-barrier surface that prevents contact with floor pathogens
options.B: To wrap the newborn baby tightly to prevent sudden infant hypothermia
options.C: To cover the mother's abdomen during sterile abdominal examinations
options.D: To collect blood samples easily for laboratory testing after the delivery

explanation: Delivery floors and unsterilized beds carry lots of germs. The plastic sheet acts as a trusty barrier to keep things clean and safe for mama. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T008#GNS226_U3_T008_h1)

question: Why does stopping your antibiotics halfway through a course cause drug resistance?

options.A: It immediately destroys all friendly bacteria inside the stomach
options.B: It causes the remaining tablets in the pack to expire faster
options.C: It triggers an allergic reaction when the drug is taken again
options.D: It leaves the strongest microbes alive to mutate and multiply

explanation: When you stop early, you only kill the weak germs. The tough ones survive, get smarter, and multiply—meaning that drug won't work for you next time! [learn more](GNS215_U4_T1#GNS215_U4_T1_h4)

question: Which group of workers faces the highest daily risk of exposure to bloodborne infections like HIV and Hepatitis B?

options.A: Healthcare workers
options.B: Market porters
options.C: Textile weavers
options.D: Construction laborers

explanation: As nurses, doctors, and lab staff handling needles and body fluids daily, we are right on the front line for bloodborne risks. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T6#GNS225_U7_T6_h4)

question: Why does a nurse perform a head-to-toe examination instead of only checking the patient's main complaint?

options.A: To detect subtle changes and physical signs of illness across all body systems
options.B: To fulfill hospital administrative requirements without clinical benefit
options.C: To quickly discharge the patient from the ward without delay
options.D: To avoid having to ask the patient about their medical history

explanation: Looking at the whole person helps uncover hidden issues that might be related to, or worsened by, the main complaint. [learn more](GNS112_U6_T1#GNS112_U6_T1_h1)

question: What physical sign usually shows up during the second stage of progressive asphyxia?

options.A: Complete paralysis of all four limbs
options.B: Cyanosis and muscle convulsions
options.C: Flushed skin and sudden hyperactivity
options.D: Uncontrolled high fever and sweating

explanation: As the body runs lower on oxygen, the skin turns a bluish color (cyanosis), and the oxygen-starved brain starts misfiring, leading to muscle twitching or seizures. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T1#GNS112_U7_T1_h3)

question: Which of these is NOT a physical danger faced by waste handlers in the hospital?

options.A: Potential infection from contaminated biological specimens
options.B: Routine promotion to hospital management positions
options.C: Accidental needle-stick injuries during linen sorting
options.D: Direct exposure to toxic chemical fumes from burning plastics

explanation: That's right! A promotion is a career win, not a workplace hazard. Handlers face real physical risks like injuries and toxic fumes. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T3#GNS122_U5_T3_h4)

question: Which body fluid carries the highest amount of infectious HIV?

options.A: Saliva
options.B: Blood
options.C: Sweat
options.D: Tears

explanation: Spot on! Blood, semen, and vaginal fluids have high viral loads capable of spreading HIV, unlike everyday touch or fluids like sweat and tears. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T2#GNS216_U6_T2_h2)

question: Which organ gets overwhelmed and converts surplus dietary sugars into fat?

options.A: Stomach
options.B: Kidneys
options.C: Pancreas
options.D: Liver

explanation: Your liver handles the heavy lifting when processing dietary sugars. When it gets overloaded, it converts those extra sugars directly into fat molecules. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T012#GNS227_U4_T012_h2)

question: What is the main purpose of a skilled nursing facility (SNF)?

options.A: To replace standard emergency room hospital services
options.B: To act as a daycare center for healthy older adults
options.C: To offer permanent housing without medical supervision
options.D: To provide 24-hour medical care and rehabilitation

explanation: Think of a skilled nursing facility as a place for round-the-clock care and therapy when patients are recovering or need ongoing clinical support. You've got this! [learn more](GNS324_U5_T11#GNS324_U5_T11_h1)

question: Why must patients finish every single dose of their prescribed antibiotics for a bacterial STI?

options.A: To build lifelong immunity against all future viral and bacterial strains
options.B: To ensure the laboratory test results turn negative by the next day
options.C: To ensure complete eradication of the pathogen and prevent treatment failure
options.D: To prevent the development of permanent skin discolouration

explanation: Stopping meds early just because symptoms fade leaves the toughest germs alive, leading to drug resistance. Always teach patients to finish their drugs! [learn more](GNS216_U5_T3#GNS216_U5_T3_h7)

question: A patient has a worm infection. Which white blood cell count will likely be high on their lab results?

options.A: Eosinophils
options.B: Platelets
options.C: Erythrocytes
options.D: Neutrophils

explanation: Correct! Eosinophils are the specialists specialized in fighting off parasites and calming down allergic reactions. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T1#GNS123_U4_T1_h3)

question: Why do neoplastic cells form a tumor instead of behaving normally?

options.A: They expand rapidly because they are fighting off local infections
options.B: They grow larger to replace dead tissue in the organ
options.C: They absorb too much water from surrounding blood vessels
options.D: They multiply uncontrollably due to failed growth regulation

explanation: You've got this! Normally, our body tells cells when to rest and when to divide. In a tumor, those control signals fail, and the cells just keep multiplying without stopping. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T6#GNS321_U1_T6_h1)

question: Six hours after a circumcision, you notice steady, active bleeding from the wound edge. What is your FIRST nursing action?

options.A: Soak the entire genital area in warm soapy bath water

options.D: Wait patiently to see if the bleeding stops on its own within an hour

question: What happens if a nursing unit allows its stock levels to fall below the minimum safety threshold?

options.A: The storage room becomes much cleaner and easier to clean
options.B: The hospital pharmacy saves a lot of money on bulk purchases
options.C: Expired items automatically get removed from the shelves
options.D: Patients may face dangerous delays in treatment due to shortages

explanation: Falling below minimum safety stock means the ward risks running out of crucial supplies during an emergency. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T19#GNS122_U3_T19_h4)

question: Why is it important to inspect MVA plastic syringes and canulas closely before sterilization?

options.A: To ensure the plastic has changed color indicating expiration
options.B: To check for cracks, scratches, or wear that could harbor bacteria
options.C: To verify the manufacturing country and brand name
options.D: To measure how much weight the plastic can hold under pressure

explanation: Damaged or cracked plastic instruments cannot maintain a proper vacuum and can trap microorganisms, leading to infection risks. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T010#GNS226_U5_T010_h8)

question: Which of these actions is WRONG when trying to stop the spread of respiratory viruses in a hospital?

options.A: Reusing disposable single-use gloves between multiple patients
options.B: Ensuring proper room ventilation in clinical spaces
options.C: Performing hand hygiene before and after patient contact
options.D: Cleaning high-touch environmental surfaces regularly

explanation: Single-use gloves are meant for one patient only! Reusing them is a sure way to spread germs around. You'd never make that mistake! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T12#GNS214_U1_T12_h7)

question: Your patient just came back from abdominal surgery. Their tummy feels a bit swollen and you can't hear any bowel sounds. What is the best nursing action?

options.A: Administer a strong laxative orally right away
options.B: Massage the abdomen vigorously to force gas out
options.C: Encourage the patient to eat a large solid meal
options.D: Keep the patient NPO until bowel activity returns

question: Why is regular self-reflection important for nurses working in post-abortion care?

options.A: It guarantees promotion to senior nursing administrative positions
options.B: It replaces the need for formal clinical pharmacology training
options.C: It helps nurses recognize their personal biases and prevent them from affecting care
options.D: It ensures the nurse never experiences physical fatigue on duty

explanation: Checking in with our own feelings helps us separate personal beliefs from professional duty, keeping our care fair and respectful. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T025#GNS226_U5_T025_h7)

question: A surgical ward is over budget mostly because staff are working too much overtime. What should the nurse manager do first?

options.A: Refuse to admit any new patients until the end of the fiscal year.
options.B: Transfer all experienced senior nurses to outpatient administrative desks.
options.C: Immediately stop purchasing all sterile surgical gloves and basic dressings.
options.D: Evaluate current staffing patterns and optimize scheduling to cover shifts efficiently.

explanation: Smart scheduling fixes the root of the problem! Fixing how shifts are covered stops excessive overtime without cutting corners on patient safety. [learn more](GST321_U1_T24#GST321_U1_T24_h4)

question: When should you as a nurse hold off on bladder irrigation unless the doctor specifically says it's okay?

options.A: When there is suspected trauma to the urinary tract

options.C: When cloudy urine appears in the clear drainage tubing
options.D: When the patient reports mild burning around the meatus

explanation: Safety first! If the urinary tract is injured, pushing fluid in can force bacteria and fluid straight out into the pelvic tissue through the tear. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T23#GNS212_U1_T23_h2)

question: A community nurse meets resistance from male elders who think family planning promotes promiscuity. What is the best first step?

options.A: Ignore the elders completely and hand out contraceptives secretly behind their backs
options.B: Engage the men in respectful dialogue, emphasizing child spacing, maternal health, and family financial stability
options.C: Argue with them aggressively to prove that their traditional beliefs are entirely wrong
options.D: Report the entire village community to the local police station immediately

explanation: Community health nursing requires patience and respect. Sitting down to talk with community leaders helps frame family planning around health, peace, and family well-being. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T1#GNS225_U3_T1_h6)

question: What is the most dangerous situation where a barium enema must NEVER be done?

options.A: Well-controlled high blood pressure
options.B: Suspected or known tear (perforation) in the gut
options.C: Mild internal piles without bleeding
options.D: A history of mild, ongoing constipation

explanation: If barium leaks out through a hole in the bowel, it causes severe and dangerous inflammation inside the abdomen. Safety first! [learn more](GNS212_U1_T9#GNS212_U1_T9_h3)

question: What are the tiny calcium crystals in the utricle and saccule called?

options.A: Ampullae
options.B: Cupulas
options.C: Otoliths
options.D: Maculae

explanation: Otoliths are like tiny microscopic stones that add weight so gravity can pull on the jelly layer and help us feel motion. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T8#GNS211_U4_T8_h4)

question: An elderly patient with arthritis uses a walking frame, but their small room is packed with heavy furniture. What should you do first?

options.A: Instruct the patient to stop using the walker immediately
options.B: Report the housing conditions to local law enforcement
options.C: Advise the patient to move to a skilled nursing facility today
options.D: Help rearrange and clear pathways to allow safe walker passage

explanation: Clearing pathways is a simple, practical step that immediately makes moving around safer without taking away the patient's independence. [learn more](GNS324_U2_T8#GNS324_U2_T8_h2)

question: Which set of lab tests is primarily ordered to check how well the thyroid gland is working?

options.A: Serum sodium and potassium levels
options.B: Morning cortisol and ACTH levels
options.C: Fasting glucose and HbA1c levels
options.D: TSH, T3, and T4 levels

explanation: Spot on! Checking TSH (the boss hormone from the pituitary) along with T3 and T4 (the actual thyroid hormones) gives a complete picture of thyroid health. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T14#GNS222_U2_T14_h7)

question: What do we call the process when cancer cells break away and travel to other parts of the body?

options.A: Apoptosis
options.B: Hyperplasia
options.C: Metastasis
options.D: Initiation

explanation: Metastasis is just the medical term for cancer packing its bags and traveling through the blood or lymph to start a new tumor elsewhere. You're mastering the terms! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T15#GNS214_U1_T15_h2)

question: Why must you carefully educate a patient about the drug that caused their idiosyncratic reaction?

options.A: To help the patient learn how to manufacture the medicine at home
options.B: To prevent accidental re-exposure to the same dangerous drug in the future
options.C: So the patient can demand financial compensation from the pharmacy
options.D: So the patient can share the leftover pills with family members

explanation: If a patient takes that same drug again later, their body will react even faster and much more severely. Clear patient teaching keeps them safe for life! [learn more](GNS125_U5_T9#GNS125_U5_T9_h6)

question: Why is psychological safety so important for nurses on the ward?

options.A: It allows nurses to skip mandatory documentation and charting duties
options.B: It gives them the confidence to speak up about safety hazards without fear
options.C: It completely eliminates all physical stress and burnout on the ward
options.D: It prevents patients from asking difficult questions about their care

explanation: When nurses feel psychologically safe, they won't hesitate to question a dodgy doctor's order or report a near-miss, and that saves lives! [learn more](GNS312_U5_T5#GNS312_U5_T5_h7)

question: When the baby's head is tucked down nicely (fully flexed), what is the measurement of the suboccipitobregmatic diameter?

options.D: 9.5 cm

question: In a female body, which organs make up the 'gonads' part of the HPG axis?

options.A: The mammary glands
options.B: The fallopian tubes
options.C: The uterus
options.D: The ovaries

question: A patient comes in with a suspected blood clot in their leg vein (deep vein thrombosis). What scan will the doctor likely order?

options.A: Renal B-Mode ultrasound
options.B: Pelvic M-Mode ultrasound
options.C: Cardiac echocardiogram
options.D: Vascular Doppler ultrasound

question: Which of these steps must you always do first before disinfecting or sterilizing equipment?

options.B: Cleaning
options.C: Disinfection
options.D: Sterilization

question: What kind of genetic inheritance pattern does sickle cell anaemia follow?

options.A: Autosomal dominant
options.B: Autosomal recessive
options.C: X-linked dominant
options.D: Mitochondrial inheritance

explanation: It's autosomal recessive! This means a child needs to inherit two faulty genes—one from each parent—to actually have the disease. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T8#GNS313_U3_T8_h2)

question: What is a key sign of an authentic leader in clinical practice?

options.A: Hiding mistakes made by senior medical personnel
options.B: Pretending to have clinical skills one does not possess
options.C: Transparent, ethical behavior and genuine self-awareness
options.D: Focusing exclusively on financial profit for the hospital

explanation: Authentic leaders build real trust because they are honest, stay true to their ethics, and aren't afraid to be real with their team. [learn more](GST321_U3_T2#GST321_U3_T2_h7)

question: What is the main reason a nurse studies a community before starting a project?

options.A: To design interventions that fit the local culture and communication channels

options.C: To collect personal taxes from every resident in the neighborhood
options.D: To write a detailed history book about the town's founding families

explanation: Checking out the community first ensures your health program makes sense for the people living there. [learn more](GNS225_U1_T3#GNS225_U1_T3_h7)

question: A family tells their young boy not to cry because 'boys must be strong.' What does this show?

options.A: A congenital developmental delay
options.B: A normal physiological reflex
options.C: An innate hormonal imbalance
options.D: The transmission of gender norms

explanation: You nailed it! Families and communities pass down gender expectations every day by teaching children how they 'should' express their feelings. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T3#GNS312_U4_T3_h3)

question: Which of these is NOT a barrier to patient education?

options.B: Severe pain and physical fatigue

question: How does assertiveness improve teamwork among different healthcare professionals?

question: What do we mean by the term 'polypharmacy'?

question: Why does a nurse listen to the chest with a stethoscope during a respiratory assessment?

question: Why might a surgeon need to perform a craniectomy (removing a piece of the skull) after severe brain trauma?

question: What is the proper way to clean the delicate lens on an infrared thermometer?

options.B: Spray high-pressure air directly onto the glass
options.C: Scrub the lens firmly with a scouring pad
options.D: Wipe gently with an approved alcohol wipe following maker instructions

explanation: A gentle wipe with isopropyl alcohol cleans the lens safely without scratching the glass or frying the electronics. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T14#GNS212_U4_T14_h7)

question: Which type of food is best for adding bulk to stool and keeping constipation away?

options.A: Refined sugars and simple carbohydrates
options.B: High-fiber foods like vegetables and whole grains
options.C: Red meats and processed sausages
options.D: Highly processed dairy products

explanation: Fiber is a superstar! It adds bulk and softness to stool, helping things move smoothly through the bowels. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T12#GNS213_U3_T12_h2)

question: A 14-year-old pregnant girl is in active labor with a narrow pelvis. What major complication is she most at risk for?

options.A: Chronic autoimmune kidney failure
options.B: Obstructed labor and potential fistula formation
options.C: Sudden adult-onset diabetes mellitus
options.D: Permanent hearing loss from high blood pressure

explanation: Exactly! An immature pelvis makes it hard for the baby to pass safely, leading to long, blocked labor and tissue injury. Early care can save lives here. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T13#GNS312_U1_T13_h2)

question: A patient is in the secretory phase of her cycle. Which hormone is doing the heavy lifting to keep this phase going?

options.A: FSH
options.B: GnRH
options.C: Testosterone
options.D: Progesterone

explanation: During the secretory phase, progesterone takes center stage to keep the uterine lining rich, thick, and cozy for a fertilized egg. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T4#GNS121_U5_T4_h4)

question: What kind of infectious agent causes Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease (CJD)?

options.A: A slow-acting bacterial spore
options.B: An abnormally folded prion protein
options.C: A parasitic protozoan in brain tissue
options.D: A mutant strand of DNA virus

explanation: Spot on! CJD is caused by prions, which are unique proteins that misfold and don't even carry DNA or RNA. You've got this! [learn more](GNS222_U4_T5#GNS222_U4_T5_h1)

question: In Nigeria, what do we mean by the 'double burden of disease'?

options.A: Having two different types of cancer simultaneously in one organ
options.B: Paying double taxes for healthcare services in public and private hospitals
options.C: Dealing with both infectious diseases and non-communicable diseases at the same time
options.D: Experiencing high rates of both malaria and severe malnutrition

explanation: Spot on! The double burden means our communities are fighting traditional infectious diseases (like malaria) while also seeing a sharp rise in chronic illnesses (like hypertension and diabetes). [learn more](GNS313_U3_T1#GNS313_U3_T1_h1)

question: A patient asks why a food with a high glycemic index can sometimes still be eaten in small amounts. What is the best nursing response?

options.A: The glycemic index only applies to people who do not take insulin.
options.B: Glycemic load looks at actual portion size, so a small serving has less overall impact.
options.C: Small amounts of high GI foods completely cure insulin resistance.
options.D: High GI foods automatically turn into low GI foods if you chew them slowly.

explanation: Glycemic load combines the GI score with the actual amount of food eaten, giving a realistic picture of blood sugar impact. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T012#GNS227_U6_T012_h3)

question: What postnatal sign shows that the uterus is slow to shrink back down to its normal pre-pregnancy size?

options.A: Increased breast engorgement
options.B: Elevated maternal temperature
options.C: Uterine subinvolution
options.D: Rapid lochia cessation

explanation: Subinvolution is just a medical term for when the womb takes way too long to go back to its normal size and tone, often leading to longer-than-normal bleeding. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T008#GNS226_U4_T008_h8)

question: What is the main reason nurses use a portable bladder scanner at the bedside?

options.A: To measure the exact blood flow to the bladder wall
options.B: To estimate the volume of urine left inside the bladder
options.C: To check the chemical composition of the urine
options.D: To look for physical stones inside the kidneys

explanation: A bladder scanner uses harmless sound waves to check how much urine is trapped inside without sticking anything in. Super handy clinical tool! [learn more](GNS212_U1_T16#GNS212_U1_T16_h4)

question: What happens when you mix two bases that don't go together?

options.A: The mixture separates and delivers an uneven dose
options.B: The mixture instantly cures all skin infections
options.C: The chemical formula permanently turns into a solid block
options.D: The active medication becomes twice as strong

explanation: If bases don't match, they split apart, meaning some parts of the cream will have too much drug and others too little. You've got this! [learn more](GNS122_U1_T20#GNS122_U1_T20_h3)

question: What is the main reason pregnant women get carpal tunnel syndrome in the third trimester?

options.A: A sudden tumor growth inside the carpal tunnel space
options.B: Permanent calcium deficiency destroying the bones of the wrist
options.C: Severe inflammation caused by repetitive typing work
options.D: Fluid retention causing tissue swelling that compresses the median nerve

explanation: Extra body fluid in late pregnancy swells the tissues inside the tight wrist space, pressing on the median nerve. Simple as that! [learn more](GNS121_U7_T6#GNS121_U7_T6_h5)

question: Why does community health nursing focus so much on wellness promotion compared to hospital care?

options.A: Because hospitals only treat infectious diseases rather than chronic illnesses
options.B: Because social and environmental factors heavily shape overall health outcomes
options.C: Because public health laws strictly forbid treating patients inside wards
options.D: Because individual patients refuse to visit clinics until they are very sick

explanation: You got this! When we look beyond just symptoms, we see that where people live, eat, and work plays a huge role in their health. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T7#GNS225_U2_T7_h1)
